classification.difficultyReason: Use equal opposite sides of a rectangle to form two equations, then solve by elimination and substitution.

content.prompt: Find the values of $a$ and $b$ in the diagram shown.

spec.description: Unshaded wide rectangle with four right-angle markers and exterior side labels. Ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black under house style.
spec.answerVisibility: All four side labels and corner markers are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal:
$$\begin{align*}3a+2b&=13 &&(1)\\2a-b&=4 &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Multiplying equation (2) by 2 and adding to equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}4a-2b&=8\\7a&=21\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Substituting into equation (2):
$$\begin{align*}2(3)-b&=4\\6-b&=4\\b&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $3(3)+2(2)=13$ and $2(3)-2=4$. Therefore, $a=3$ and $b=2$.
